version.note: The original work is for solo piano. The exact edition or performing copy used by Moiseiwitsch is not identified. The viewed Fromont score establishes the written structure; no cut, edition variant, pedal execution or bar-exact performance claim is inferred from the file’s duration.

performers.note: The primary label and item identify the solo pianist; the matching session chronology corroborates him.

date.note: The chronology’s BM-C#051 entry gives 28 February 1946 and matrix 2EA10890-1, matching the selected carrier. The source is secondary; no independently accessible DAHR session entry was established. The item’s year 1946 is not itself treated as a day-level session date.

place.note: The venue is explicitly named in the matching matrix entry, not inferred from HMV’s address or the performer’s residence.

label.note: Original British 12-inch 78-rpm disc; Made in England and speed 78 appear on the viewed label.

catalogue.note: The original label identifies C.3485. Internet Archive assigns the item the catalogue year 1946; the label does not print that date and a contemporary release notice has not been established.

matrixTakeSides.value: 2EA10890-1; label matrix 2EA.10890; Clair de lune side of HMV C.3485
matrixTakeSides.note: The -1 take identifier is supplied by the runout/item metadata and matches the session chronology. The other side is Chopin’s Polonaise in B♭, op. 71 no. 2. GBIA3042373B is the repository identifier, not a claim that the label prints a B-side designation. No alternative take is substituted; DAHR corroboration remains unavailable.

credits.value: George Blood, L.P.; transfer by Phoebe Pugh; cleaning by Levar Brown
credits.note: The item explicitly credits user_transferred Phoebe Pugh and user_cleaned Levar Brown. The preferred version was selected by an unnamed George Blood audio engineer; that person is not identified with the uploader.

date.note: No transfer date is explicitly stated. The 2024 repository public/added dates and file modification times are not promoted to a transfer date.

processing.value: 78-rpm transfer; preferred 3.5mil ET stylus version, equalised with Turnover 375 and Rolloff −12; VBR MP3 derived from the preferred 24-bit FLAC
processing.note: The item describes four stylus transfers, but the exact selected friendly-named FLAC comment identifies 3.5mil ET with the stated equalisation. The MP3 names that FLAC as its source. Further noise reduction, pitch correction, editing and restoration settings are not documented.

digital.format: VBR MP3 access derivative of George Blood’s preferred equalised 3.5mil ET transfer, supplied as 24-bit FLAC

composition.value: Underlying composition is out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies.
composition.note: Debussy died in 1918; the suite was published in 1905. This is territorial composition-term reasoning, not worldwide clearance or clearance of an unidentified modern performing edition.

recording.value: Rule 3 — EU public-domain term basis for a phonogram published before 1963; territorial, not worldwide.
recording.note: The selected HMV C.3485 item is catalogued as published in 1946. That catalogue year, rather than the session date alone, supplies the pre-1963 publication basis. Its earlier 50-year phonogram term had expired before the 1 November 2013 extension threshold. US sound-recording status is not established. No Creative Commons licence or worldwide public-domain dedication is claimed.

rights.creditLine: Claude Debussy, Suite bergamasque, III. Clair de lune; Benno Moiseiwitsch, piano. Recorded 28 February 1946, Abbey Road Studio 3, London; His Master’s Voice C.3485, matrix 2EA10890-1, item catalogued 1946. George Blood, L.P. transfer by Phoebe Pugh, via Internet Archive. Rule 3 territorial EU basis; US status not established.

sources.locator: Item metadata: Benno Moiseiwitsch, piano; Suite bergamasque no. 3; His Master’s Voice C.3485; catalogue date 1946; matrix 2EA10890-1; George Blood transfer project and Phoebe Pugh credit. The 2024 public and added dates are repository dates.

sources.title: His Master’s Voice — original C.3485 label and runout image
sources.locator: Viewed original label: Made in England, speed 78, C.3485, 2EA.10890, Benno Moiseiwitsch, pianoforte solo, No. 3 from Suite Bergamasque. The runout and item metadata identify 2EA10890-1. The label itself does not print a publication date.

sources.title: Internet Archive — selected transfer and derivative provenance
sources.locator: Friendly-named preferred FLAC: 24-bit FLAC, 259.86 seconds; comment identifies the 3.5mil ET stylus and equalisation Turnover 375, Rolloff −12. The exact selected friendly-named MP3 is its VBR access derivative. This is not a switch to another transfer.

sources.title: Classical Pianists — Benno Moiseiwitsch recording chronology
sources.locator: Entry BM-C#051: 28 February 1946, Abbey Road Studio 3, London, England; Debussy Clair de lune; matrix 2EA10890-1, mastered. The matrix matches the selected primary carrier. This is secondary session documentation, not a DAHR record.

sources.title: Discography of American Historical Recordings — consultation
sources.locator: DAHR homepage consulted; performer/title and exact matrix searches did not yield an identifiable entry for British HMV 2EA10890. The direct interactive route presented an access challenge. No DAHR session, take or release corroboration is claimed; this does not establish that the database contains no relevant entry.

sources.title: Sibley Music Library — Suite bergamasque, E. Fromont, 1905
sources.locator: Library record identifies Debussy (1862–1918), the 1905 Paris Fromont edition, piano score, public-domain access and contents: Prélude, Menuet, Clair de lune, Passepied. Persistent identifier: http://hdl.handle.net/1802/12331.

sources.title: Debussy — Suite bergamasque, 1905 Fromont score
sources.locator: Viewed Clair de lune on printed/PDF pp. 14–19, plate E. 1404 F.: D♭ major, 9/8, Andante très expressif; chordal opening, Tempo rubato, un poco mosso, Calmato, a Tempo I and morendo. This is evidence for the written work, not the performing copy used at the 1946 session.

sources.title: IMSLP — Suite bergamasque, CD 82 (L. 75)
sources.locator: Work information: four movements; 1890–1905 composition/revision history; June 1905 publication; Clair de lune is movement III, not a self-contained one-movement suite.

sources.title: Paul Verlaine — Clair de lune, Fêtes galantes
sources.locator: Viewed poem in the 1891 Vanier edition, pp. 5–6: masks and bergamasques, lute, dancing, uncertain happiness, moonlight and fountains. The poem first appeared in Fêtes galantes in 1869; the separate work page identifies that publication. Used as literary context, not a bar-by-bar programme.

sources.title: Wikisource — Verlaine’s Clair de lune, publication identification
sources.locator: Identifies the poem as part of Fêtes galantes (1869); the opened 1891 text is a later edition of the poem.

sources.title: Directive 2006/116/EC — copyright and related-rights terms
sources.locator: Articles 1, 3 and 8: ordinary composition term and pre-extension phonogram terms and calendar calculation. Territorial term reasoning, not a licence.

sources.title: Directive 2011/77/EU — phonogram term extension
sources.locator: Article 1(3), inserting Article 10(5): the extended terms concern recordings still protected on 1 November 2013; Article 2 gives the implementation date. Earlier expired terms are not revived by this rule.
